titre: Modals: must, have to, should, might

piege.titre: must not is not the same as do not have to

q.lu: All employees must ------- their badges at the entrance.

etapes.texte: After a modal: the **base verb**, nothing else
__must not__ = forbidden. __do not have to__ = not necessary

phrases.texte: Modal verbs: must, have to, should and might.
A modal verb changes the meaning of the main verb. Must and have to express an obligation: visitors must sign in.
phrases.dit: A modal verb changes the meaning of the main verb. Must, and have to, express an obligation: visitors must sign in.

phrases.texte: Should gives advice: you should book early.
phrases.dit: Should, gives advice: you should book early.

phrases.texte: Might and may express a possibility: the flight might be late.
phrases.dit: Might, and may, express a possibility: the flight might be late.

phrases.texte: The form is simple. After a modal, we use the base verb. No to.
phrases.dit: The form is simple. After a modal, we use the base verb. No to.

phrases.texte: And no S, even with he or she.
phrases.dit: And no S, even with he, or she.

phrases.texte: We say: she must sign the form.
Now, the big trap. Must not means it is forbidden: you must not park here.
phrases.dit: Now, the big trap. Must not, means it is forbidden: you must not park here.

phrases.texte: But do not have to means it is not necessary. You do not have to come: you can choose.
phrases.dit: But, do not have to, means it is not necessary. You do not have to come: you can choose.

phrases.texte: Now, a TOEIC question. All employees must, blank, their badges at the entrance.
A: show. B: to show. C: showing. D: shows.
phrases.dit: Answer A. show. Answer B. to show. Answer C. showing. Answer D. shows.

phrases.texte: The word before the blank is must, a modal. After a modal, only the base verb is possible.
phrases.dit: The word before the blank is must, a modal. After a modal, only the base verb is possible.

phrases.texte: So B, C and D are wrong.
phrases.dit: So B, C, and D are wrong.

phrases.texte: A is correct: all employees must show their badges at the entrance.
Three steps. One: after a modal, the base verb, nothing else.
Two: must is an obligation, should is advice, might is a possibility.
phrases.dit: Two: must, is an obligation. Should, is advice. Might, is a possibility.

phrases.texte: Three: must not means forbidden. Do not have to means not necessary.
phrases.dit: Three: must not, means forbidden. Do not have to, means not necessary.
